about.main:
About

About RHAGF

Who we are

We are a non-profit and voluntary organization established with the aim to builds hope, love, respect and transformation for those impacted by sexual exploitation and sex trafficking in Nigeria and other Places. We do this in three strategies: heal the harm; build for the future; and champion social equality. We offer counseling, court support, workshops, education bursaries, and other supports as these people may need. We also address issues relating to behavioral health, i.e. substance abuse, Alcohol and Drug addiction, Serious Psychological distress, Suicide and re-occurring incidence in Nigerian and beyond, provide a platform for women, youth and other stakeholders in education, peace sectors, religious institutes and others, as well as liaise and initiate projects to facilitate the quest for quality long life for all Nigerians and across the world

Learn More

Become a Volunteers

Join your hand with us for a
better life and future

Discover More
Know more about us

Change the world with us

“RHAGF offers counseling, court support, workshops, education bursaries, and other supports as these people may need. We are a non-profit and voluntary organization established with the aim to builds hope, love, respect and transformation for those impacted by sexual exploitation and sex trafficking in Nigeria and other Places”

Learn how to get help

OUR MISSION

We seek to transform and improve the quality of life among slum dwellers who face different challenges ranging from extreme poverty, poor health, human trafficking recruitment, drug abuse and peddling, sexual abuse, sexual exploitation and sex trafficking, illegal migration, out of school children and girl child education.

OUR VISION

We envision a Nigeria where there is hope, respect and transformation of individuals, families and communities to live more meaningful, purposeful and productive life of inclusion, self sustaining and independence which eventually translates to National development.

The Regy&Henry Amazing Grace Foundation is set to implement its fifth year of the Slum to School project on SEPTEMBER 9, 2025, at LEA Primary School Mabushi. Here’s a summary of the project’s progress and goals:

Project Overview

The Slum to School project aims to provide education to underprivileged children in slum communities, addressing issues like poverty, illiteracy, and lack of access to quality education.

Achievements

  • Over the past four years, the project has impacted verifiable 400 children and 400 households in communities like Kute, Dusape, kuchikaw, Sumpe, Shishipe 1, Shishipe 2, Garuywi, Torge; Kuryomi and Gosa in Abuja,FCT Nigeria.
  • The foundation has provided enrollment fees,school bags, sandals, and books to support these children.
  • Parents and caregivers of program beneficiaries have been trained in various skills to help them financially support their children’s education.¹

Fifth-Year Goals

  • The project aims to reach another 100 out-of-school children and indigent families.
